principles: Protect all N3/N4 questions, every browser review record, every teacher edit timestamp and all questions in any finalised concept, including a concept with no questions.
Prefer concise exam-style listening tasks that identify the specific feature, without naming the answer or inventing an audible event.
Use plausible alternatives from the same musical task. Prefer own-level concepts only when they make useful distractors; earlier-level terms can be better than an unrelated own-level term.
Exclude equivalent alternatives and known coexisting answers using the library tags and Dictionary relationships.
Retire repetitive written identification and duplicated two-statement checks where the retained definition and listening tasks already assess the fact. Do not fill a six-question quota.
Retain specialist vocabulary, correct-answer IDs, typed variants, recordings, timing, saved edits and finalisation. Definitions should be concise and give useful musical context.
